items.title: Claude Code sends 33k tokens before reading the prompt; OpenCode sends 7k
items.raw_content: This started based off of a hunch. We usually use OpenCode, but were 'forced' to use Claude Code for a while due to issues with Meridian. In that time, we saw the usage meter rise much, much more quickly than when using OpenCode. This was the initial anecdotal evidence, but we undertook this small study to collect empirical data: We added logging between the agentic coding tool (Claude Code and OpenCode) and Anthropic's endpoint, and captured all requests (and the returned usage blocks). With one caveat (toward the end of the post) we found unambiguously that Claude Code was far more inefficient in terms of its cache strategy and its harness token usage than OpenCode.
items.title_zh: Claude Code 读取提示前已发送 3.3 万 token，OpenCode 仅 7000
items.summary: A small study that logged traffic between agentic coding tools and Anthropic's endpoint found Claude Code was markedly less efficient in its cache strategy and harness token usage than OpenCode, with one caveat noted at the end.

items.title: Ghostel.el: Terminal emulator powered by libghostty
items.raw_content: Ghostel is an Emacs terminal emulator powered by libghostty-vt - the same VT engine that drives the Ghostty terminal. A native dynamic module written in Zig handles terminal state, rendering, and local PTY I/O; Elisp manages keymaps, buffers, commands, and remote process integration. Ghostel is inspired by emacs-libvterm and follows the same two-layer design, but uses Ghostty's modern VT engine instead of libvterm. This brings the Kitty keyboard and graphics protocols, rich underline styles, OSC 8 hyperlinks, OSC 4/10/11 color queries, and synchronized output (DEC 2026) - none of which libvterm supports. See Ghostel vs vterm and eat for a detailed comparison.
items.title_zh: Ghostel.el：由 libghostty 驱动的终端模拟器
items.summary: Ghostel is an Emacs terminal emulator built on libghostty-vt, the VT engine behind Ghostty, with a native Zig module handling terminal state, rendering and local PTY I/O while Elisp manages keymaps, buffers and commands. It follows the two-layer design of emacs-libvterm but adds Kitty keyboard and graphics protocols, OSC 8 hyperlinks and synchronized output.

items.title: Don't you mean extinct?
items.raw_content: In 1993, Jurassic Park came out and revolutionized the use of CGI in films [1] . To the public the experience was magic. But for some of the people in the movie industry, it was a rude awakening. Director Steven Spielberg had hired stop-motion master [2] Phil Tippett [3] to bring the film's full-body dinosaurs to life using his go-motion technique. Spielberg was highly skeptical that computer-generated imagery (CGI) could realistically depict a dinosaur [4] . But Dennis Muren and the digital artists at Industrial Light & Magic (ILM) worked on a proof-of-concept using CGI. They rendered a fully textured, photorealistic T. rex chasing a herd of Gallimimus in full sunlight.
items.title_zh: 你不是想说“灭绝”吗？
items.summary: A retrospective on Jurassic Park's 1993 CGI breakthrough: Steven Spielberg had hired stop-motion specialist Phil Tippett to animate full-body dinosaurs, but a proof-of-concept by Dennis Muren and Industrial Light & Magic rendered a fully textured, photorealistic T. rex chase, a rude awakening for parts of the industry.

items.title: How to read more books
items.raw_content: I’ve read roughly a book a week for a few years, and I can tell you it’s doable. I didn’t always read this much. When I started, I read fewer than ten volumes per year, but making it a goal made me switch gears and achieve what I once thought was impossible. I want to explain what I did to become a prolific reader, and what I learned in the process, so that, with a bit of effort, you can do it too. I promise, it will be worth it. First of all, you don’t have to make time to read. What you need to do is read every single time you are not doing something else. In today’s world, most people pick up their phones as soon as they get a moment of inactivity. Serious readers pick up their books instead. So an effective way is to replace the time you spend in front of a screen, like PCs, smartphones, and TVs, with time spent reading a book.
items.title_zh: 如何读更多的书
items.summary: A reader who has averaged roughly a book a week for several years explains how he went from fewer than ten books a year to that pace, chiefly by reading whenever he would otherwise reach for a screen.

items.title: Edge Physical AI Deployment of Vision Transformers on Heterogeneous Edge GPU Targeting Autonomous Vehicles
items.title_zh: 面向自动驾驶的异构边缘 GPU 视觉 Transformer 物理 AI 部署
items.summary: The paper presents Heterogeneous Frame Dispatch Scheduling (H-FraDS), which routes frames across the GPU and two DLA cores at fixed dispatch ratios and adapts accelerator-incompatible transformer components, including tensor reshaping, a tanh approximation of ERF and bounded tanh layer normalization. Using Swin Transformer for autonomous-driving perception, balanced 1:2 dispatch reports 125.93 FPS, a 2.36x speedup over adapted-DLA-only execution, 4.0 FPS/W and roughly 24 ms DLA latency.

items.title: Bandit PCA with Minimax Optimal Regret
items.title_zh: 具有极小极大最优遗憾的 Bandit PCA
items.summary: The paper studies bandit-feedback online principal component analysis, where an adversary selects a rank-r symmetric gain matrix with spectrum in [0,1] each round and the learner chooses a unit vector, and establishes a minimax regret of order r times the square root of dT up to polylogarithmic factors, improving on both prior bounds. The upper bound comes from an algorithm combining online mirror descent on the density-matrix spectrahedron with multiscale exploration, and the lower bound from an adaptive adversary.

items.title: WSqD: A Horizon-Free Learning Rate Schedule for Large Model Training
items.title_zh: WSqD：面向大模型训练的免视界学习率调度
items.summary: WSqD replaces the constant stable phase of warmup-stable-decay with a shifted inverse-square-root base schedule while keeping a final linear cooldown, making the base schedule horizon-independent so the horizon is needed only to decide when cooldown begins. It is proved to attain the minimax-optimal O(1/sqrt(T)) last-iterate rate in the stochastic convex setting, and in SlimPajama language-model pretraining it matches or outperforms tuned WSD and other baselines across horizons while reusing a single peak learning rate.

items.title: ChipVerilog: A Large-Scale OpenCores-Derived Benchmark for LLM-Based Verilog RTL Generation
items.title_zh: ChipVerilog：基于 OpenCores 的大规模 LLM Verilog RTL 生成基准
items.summary: ChipVerilog is a description-to-Verilog benchmark built from OpenCores IP and core designs, containing 64 generation targets across OR1200, a double-precision FPU, MIPS-16, I2C and CORDIC, including cross-module targets and several exceeding 1,000 lines of Verilog. Generated RTL is checked by compilation and validated by equivalence checking for local modules or by simulation for integrated IP and core targets, and results show large-scale hierarchical RTL remains challenging.

items.title: The Singularity Space: A Generative Diffusion Framework for Signal Representation
items.title_zh: 奇点空间：一种用于信号表示的生成式扩散框架
items.summary: Singularity Space represents signals through complex-plane pole-residue singularities instead of dense amplitude grids, learning a latent space of physically constrained per-signal singularity configurations with a transformer-based diffusion model that predicts singularity coordinates subject to geometric constraints during sampling. On 1D Burgers shocks, 32 predicted singularities per shock replace a 1024-point grid, preserving structure under unseen observation noise and reporting 4.2x lower reconstruction error than a grid-based baseline in zero-shot sub-resolution generalization.

items.title: ARMOR-IMC: Adaptive Resource Mapping for Operational Robustness via Secure In-Memory Computing
items.title_zh: ARMOR-IMC：通过安全存内计算实现运行鲁棒性的自适应资源映射
items.summary: The paper presents a post-training framework that hardens analog in-memory computing accelerators based on SOT-MTJs against process variation and power side-channel attacks simultaneously, using a Variation Impact Score to guide the mapping of Fault Observation Windows and a Leakage Per Inference metric to quantify input-dependent power variability. Implemented in the IMAC-Sim simulator, it is reported to restore near-baseline accuracy where process-variation faults degrade accuracy by more than 50%, while mitigating correlation-based power analysis.
